name: Synth sounds
summary: Synthesized sound in rules and feedback: notes with a wave shape, pitch slides and short jingles, with pitch from an expression. Every sound in a game is synthesized.
when_to_use: Any game that plays notes or sound effects: instruments, pads, ambient tones, rhythm feedback.
api: feedback {sound: {wave, note, ms, slide?, volume?}} or {sound: {wave, notes, step_ms}}; note may be Hz from an expression
notes: maps to synth_sound (engine v0.2 feedback sound); authoring/SPEC.md 2.9: all sound is synthesized

name: Melody player
summary: Plays a short synthesized melody or sound on cue: a jingle from a note list (one wave, even steps), or a rendered melody clip (melody_clip) with chords, bass and drums, so a game can play a prompt the player then answers.
when_to_use: Listen-then-answer games with original melodies or tones: repeat the tune, which interval, tempo guessing.
api: feedback {sound: {wave, notes: [..], step_ms}} triggered by a rule, notes from content or an expression; or feedback {sound: {asset: "clip_<i>"}} for a melody_clip (the asset may be an expression); the play_clip fragment wires a clip to each quiz question
notes: jingles map to synth_sound; clips to melody_clip and play_clip. Recorded clips, real songs and voices are not available (see audio_clip); content must be original melodies

name: Melody clips
summary: Short original music clips the model writes as notes (a lead line, chords, an optional bass line and drums) with an era style (50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s, 00s, 10s, chip, baroque or plain) that picks the instruments, groove and recording colour. The expander renders each clip at build time into a WAV sound asset clip_<i>, so the game ships its audio and replays stay exact.
when_to_use: Listen-and-answer content: guess the decade or genre by ear, which instrument, name the jingle, sound pairs, pitch and interval quizzes with real chords. Use with play_clip for a clip per quiz question, or play a clip from any feedback with {sound: {asset: "clip_3"}}. Write original tunes only; never a real song's melody.
api: manifest sound.clips: [clip, ...] (up to 12, each under 10 s, all under 80 s; over 30 s of clips they are stored 8-bit). clip = {style: 50s|60s|70s|80s|90s|00s|10s|chip|baroque|plain, bpm 50-200, bars 1-8, meter 4|3, lead: "A4/8 C5 E5 r/4 G5/2" (note+octave or r, durations /1 /2 /4 /8 /16, dotted /4., a duration carries to the next notes), chords: "Am F C G" (one per bar, or Am/2; m 7 maj7 m7 m7b5 dim dim7 aug sus2 sus4 add9 6 m6 9 5), bass: auto|none|root|root8|octave|walk|root_fifth|offbeat|sub|notes, drums: auto|none|shuffle|backbeat|disco|gated|house|breakbeat|rnb|trap|chip|waltz|{kick, snare, hat, open, clap, tamb, rim: "x...X..."}, lead_sound|chord_sound|bass_sound: sine triangle square pulse chip saw supersaw brass strings pad organ piano epiano bell pluck harpsichord flute bass synth_bass fm_bass sub chip_bass, comp: pad stabs offbeat strum arp boogie block, swing 0-1, label}. Clip i becomes asset clip_<i>; play it with feedback {sound: {asset: "clip_<i>"}} or an expression like "= 'clip_' + str(event.clip)". Errors A_SOUND_CLIP at /sound/clips/<i>/<field>.

params.style: enum, default plain: 50s 60s 70s 80s 90s 00s 10s chip baroque plain
params.bars: int, default 4, 1..8 (the clip must stay under 10 s)
params.lead: string of notes, up to 128 tokens
params.chords: string of chord symbols, up to 64
params.drums: groove name, auto, none or a pattern object

gaps_it_closes: all sound is synthesized; no recorded clips
no way to play a different tune per question
notes: Rendered by the expander (pure JS, no Math.sin/exp/random), so the same clip is the same bytes in Node and JavaScriptCore. Presentation only: the engine never reads audio. Real songs, recordings and voices stay out (audio_clip, tts_audio). Muse writes valid notation first try (16/16 clips in two real-Muse runs); era identity comes mostly from the style, so ask for era rhythm explicitly. docs/harness-gaps/audio.md.

name: Metronome
summary: A steady beat: a timer fires every beat interval, plays a tick and advances a beat counter that other rules sync to.
when_to_use: Music making, rhythm games, step sequencers and anything played to a tempo.
api: timers every <ms per beat> → incr beat; feedback synth tick; tempo changes use self-rescheduling after timers
notes: custom rules from timers (every / after) and synth_sound; no fragment yet. every takes a constant, so a changing tempo uses after

name: Step sequencer grid
summary: A grid of on/off cells (rows are sounds, columns are steps) that plays back in a loop: a playhead moves one column per beat and triggers the rows that are on.
when_to_use: Beat makers, drum pattern copying, step-based music puzzles.
api: grid_board for toggles (tap_cell → set_at); metronome timer moves the playhead; per-row synth sound when a cell under the playhead is on
notes: custom rules from grid_board (up to 10 x 10), timers, grid builtins and synth_sound

name: Piano-roll grid
summary: A pitch-by-time grid: place notes on rows (pitches in a scale) and columns (steps), then play the melody back.
when_to_use: Melody composing, harmonizing and transcription games.
api: grid_board cells (row = pitch, column = step); playback timer plays synth notes with Hz from the row
notes: custom rules from grid_board (up to 10 x 10), timers and synth_sound (note Hz from an expression)

name: Piano keys
summary: A row of tappable keys that each play a pitch, for playing or answering with notes.
when_to_use: Repeat-the-melody, name-the-note and chord games.
api: rect nodes with on_tap {input: key, with: {i}}; rule plays synth note for key i; or the keyboard fragment with one letter per note
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and synth_sound; pairs with sequence_memory for repeat-the-tune

name: Sound pads
summary: A few big pads that each play a sound when tapped (held pads can sustain with hold buttons).
when_to_use: Soundboards, finger drumming, live jamming.
api: rect or circle nodes with on_tap / on_press; each triggers a synth sound
notes: custom rules from tap nodes, hold_buttons and synth_sound; sequence_memory already draws 3-6 toned pads

name: Haptics
summary: Phone vibration feedback on game moments: light, medium, heavy, success, warning, error.
when_to_use: Fidget, calm and tactile games, and juice on hits and wins.
api: feedback {haptic: light | medium | heavy | success | warning | error}
notes: maps to particles_haptics (engine v0.2 feedback haptic); the iOS host maps it to feedback generators

name: Hold input
summary: Hold a finger down and release it as the input: hold length or release timing is the play.
when_to_use: Breathing pacers, charge-and-release throws, hold-to-move.
api: node on_press / on_release inputs; record now at press and compare at release
notes: maps to hold_buttons (engine v0.2.1)

name: Slider
summary: A draggable handle along a track that sets a number between a minimum and maximum.
when_to_use: Mixers, budgets, colour mixing, estimates on a scale, volume and tempo controls.
api: a track rect plus a handle node with on_drag; value = clamp((pointer.x - x0) / w, 0, 1) mapped to the range
notes: custom rules from pointer_input (on_drag), clamp and lerp; no fragment yet

name: Drag into slots
summary: Drag items onto target slots; an item snaps into a slot it is dropped over, and rules check whether it is the right slot.
when_to_use: Decorating, arranging, jigsaw-like placing, matching labels to places, building from parts.
api: item nodes with on_drag move state positions; on release (on_release) snap to the slot found with overlaps_rect or nearest dist; set_at records the slot
notes: custom rules from pointer_input (on_drag), hold_buttons (on_release), overlaps_rect, dist and set_at; no fragment yet

name: Stroke recorder
summary: Records the finger's path while it is down as a list of points per stroke, and draws it back as lines; the replay log keeps it.
when_to_use: Drawing, tracing, one-stroke and draw-and-guess games.
api: inputs from {"pointer": "down" | "move" | "up"} push vec(x, y) into list state; draw each stroke with a poly node (open, up to 256 points)
notes: custom rules from pointer_input and vector_shapes; one pointer only, 256 points per poly, collection size limits apply. See drawing_canvas for a full canvas

name: Sticker set
summary: A themed set of placeable items (stickers, furniture, plants, fish), made as one sprite sheet with a frame per item and a content list of their names.
when_to_use: Dress-up, decorating, room arranging and comic building.
api: art: one sprite role with a frame per item (image frame = index); content list of item names
notes: maps to image_assets (sprite frames, as match_pairs' card sprite uses) and the art pipeline; very large sets are limited by sheet size

name: Colour palette
summary: A row of colour swatches; tapping one sets the current colour that painting rules use.
when_to_use: Colouring, pixel art, colour-by-number and design games.
api: swatch rect nodes with on_tap set state color (hex string); grid_board cell_fill returns the hex for painted cells
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and grid_board's cell_fill hex strings

name: Pixel grid
summary: A grid of cells the player paints one cell at a time with the current colour.
when_to_use: Pixel art, colour-by-number, shared pixel canvases.
api: grid_board (tap_cell → set_at on a grid or list of hex strings; cell_fill reads it)
notes: grid_board caps at 10 x 10; larger canvases need custom rect nodes over a grid() state

name: Progress meter
summary: A bar or ring that fills as a number rises toward a goal.
when_to_use: Completion in colouring, collecting and cozy games; any visible goal.
api: a rect whose w is bound (=) to progress / goal × width
notes: plain presentation binding; timer_bar and shared_progress draw similar bars

name: Cooldown
summary: After an action, it can't be used again until a cooldown passes.
when_to_use: Paced actions: placing a pixel, using a power, special moves.
api: state ready_at; guard input with now >= ready_at; set ready_at = now + cooldown
notes: within one run only (now, after timers); cooldowns across runs or across a Group need stored state (growth_timer)

name: Tap to pop
summary: A board of poppable bubbles: a tap flips one with a sound and haptic; a full board resets.
when_to_use: Fidget toys, satisfying tap boards, calm play.
api: grid_board tap_cell → set_at popped; cell_fill shows the state; feedback sound and haptic
notes: custom rules from grid_board, synth_sound and particles_haptics

name: Care buttons
summary: A few care actions (water, feed, light, prune) that raise needs meters which drain over time.
when_to_use: Plant, pet and garden care games.
api: button nodes with on_tap raise state meters; a tick or every rule drains them
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and timers, within one run. Care that continues between days needs growth_timer

name: Tap a choice
summary: A few labelled buttons; tapping one records the pick and moves on.
when_to_use: Mood check-ins, polls, simple picks without right answers.
api: button nodes with on_tap {input: pick, with: {i}}; or quiz / choice_story for longer sets
notes: plain tap nodes; quiz and choice_story already draw choice buttons

name: Letter tiles
summary: A small set of letter tiles; tap letters to spell a word, then submit it to be checked.
when_to_use: Make-words-from-these-letters games, letter hives and wheels.
api: keyboard fragment with letters = the set plus '<' and '>'; rules build typed and check in_dictionary and the required letter
notes: keyboard fragment plus the in_dictionary builtin; a hexagon layout needs custom nodes

name: Letter rack
summary: A rack of letter tiles where each tile can be used once per word; tapping moves a tile into the word and back.
when_to_use: Longest-word, anagram and unscramble games.
api: list state of tiles with a used flag; tile nodes on_tap toggle; submit checks in_dictionary or the answer
notes: custom rules from tap nodes, list builtins and in_dictionary; word_check handles fixed-length guesses

name: Word bank
summary: Shuffled word chips; tap them in order to build a sentence, then check it against the answer.
when_to_use: Translation, grammar and sentence-order games.
api: content list split into words; shuffle at start; chip nodes on_tap push to the built sentence; compare join(built, ' ')
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and split, shuffle, push, join

name: Number entry
summary: Enter a number as the answer on the iPhone keyboard, then compare it to the target (exact, closeness or higher/lower).
when_to_use: Estimation, price guessing, counts and maths answers.
api: a text input ({"text": "submit"}) with parse_int (or your own decimal parse) on the submitted value; or slider_input for a range
notes: text_input plus parse_int

name: Dice roll
summary: Rolls one or more dice with seeded randomness and shows the faces.
when_to_use: Board games, luck games, probability lessons.
api: random_int(1, 6) in an effect (rule body); show the face with text or a sprite frame
notes: maps to the random_int builtin; seeded, so replays and dailies match

name: Dice
summary: Seeded dice for roll-and-move and luck rules.
when_to_use: Roll-and-move boards and dice games.
api: random_int(1, sides) in an effect
notes: same as dice_roll; maps to random_int

name: Flashcards
summary: A deck of two-sided cards: see the front, flip to the back, then rate how well you knew it.
when_to_use: Study, vocabulary and memorization games.
api: content lists fronts and backs; tap to flip (state flipped); rating buttons move the card back in the queue
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and list builtins within one run; spacing across days needs srs_scheduler

name: Stat meters
summary: A few named numbers (HP, gold, trust, heat, stamina) clamped to a range and shown as labelled bars; rules raise and lower them and react at thresholds.
when_to_use: RPG stats, story meters, resource balancing, battle HP, reign-style balance games.
api: int or float state per meter; incr / set with clamp(); bars are rects with w bound to value / max; when-rules fire at thresholds
notes: custom rules from state, clamp and bound rect widths; the gold story games keep Clues, Trust and Heat this way. lives covers a single HP count

name: Tap hotspots
summary: Invisible or drawn tap areas placed on a scene; tapping one marks it found (a clue, a target, a difference), and taps elsewhere can cost a miss.
when_to_use: Hidden object, spot-the-difference, point-and-click clues, shooting galleries.
api: transparent rect or circle nodes (repeat over a content list of {x, y, r}) with on_tap {input: found, with: {i}}; a pointer down source catches misses
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and pointer_input; bots tap rect/circle ops, so keep a transparent rect under each sprite

name: Inventory
summary: A list of items the player holds; picking up adds one, using or combining removes them, and choices or doors check for them.
when_to_use: Escape rooms, adventure and story games with key items, crafting. In a branching story, items are story-graph vars of kind "item" (branching_story).
api: list<string> or set state; push / add on pickup, remove on use, has / contains in guards; a row of item icons in the HUD
notes: custom rules from list and set builtins; in a branching_story an item is a 0/1 var shown in the bag line and checked by a choice's "if" (story_vars hides the choice when it fails)

name: Swipe directions
summary: Reads a swipe's direction (up, down, left, right) as the input, for dodges, guards and directional answers.
when_to_use: Parry and dodge duels, directional reaction games, swipe-to-answer.
api: pointer down records the start; pointer up compares the delta: the larger axis and its sign give the direction (as tile_slide does)
notes: custom rules from pointer_input and the direction constants; tile_slide already reads swipes this way

name: Swipe cards
summary: One card at a time; swipe it left or right (or tap two buttons) to decide, and each side has its own effects.
when_to_use: Reign-like balance games, this-or-that, quick decisions with consequences.
api: card node with on_drag following the finger; release past a threshold commits left or right; content lists of card text and per-side effects
notes: custom rules from pointer_input, hold_buttons (on_release) and meters; the gold two_way_speed_sort uses two buttons plus swipe

name: Draining power
summary: A power supply that drains over time and faster for each device left on; at zero everything shuts off.
when_to_use: Night-shift survival, resource-budget horror and management games.
api: timer_bar with drain_mult raised per active device, or a meter drained in a tick rule
notes: maps to timer_bar (drain_mult, emit_only) or meters

name: Checklist
summary: A list of tasks the player completes in any order; each is ticked off, and finishing all of them wins.
when_to_use: Ritual, chore and escape tasks under a clock.
api: list<bool> state from a content list; set_at on completion; all(list, d => d) wins
notes: custom rules from list builtins (set_at, all, count)

name: Camera feeds
summary: Tap buttons to switch which room the screen shows; things keep moving in rooms you are not watching.
when_to_use: Security-camera horror, monitoring and management games.
api: state view (room index) set by button taps; the scene draws only the current room's actors from state that updates for every room in tick
notes: custom rules from tap nodes and tick_rules; not a real camera (the engine camera only scrolls one world)

name: Looking away
aliases: only moves when you look away
summary: Tracks which way the player is looking (the current view or direction); threats move only while not looked at.
when_to_use: Don't-look-away horror and freeze-tag mechanics.
api: state facing (set by swipes or buttons); threats advance in tick only when not in the facing view
notes: custom rules from swipe_zones or tap buttons and tick_rules; real eye or head tracking is not available

name: Picture choice round
summary: A multiple-choice round built around one picture per question: picture_quiz for the answers and a picture above them, either still or zooming out (zoom_reveal). The pictures are frames of one sprite: SVG drawn by Muse, or a build-time raster image.
when_to_use: Picture trivia (which animal, what landmark, whose cartoon), close-up guessing, picture rebus with choices, "what is the French cartoon saying" with a caricature of a generic character.
api: uses [zoom_reveal (zoom_from 1 for a still picture), picture_quiz, rounds bound to question_done, lives bound to answered_wrong]; game functions zoom_index = get_or(order, qi, 0), zoom_hold = locked; art.sprites.picture = {svg: [one per question], w: 512, h: 512}. Example: authoring/games/zoom_safari.authoring.json
notes: SVG pictures work today inside the 192 KB art budget (about 6 KB per frame when there are 4 or more). Raster photos need generated_image or picture_pack and a sprite sheet made at build time
